newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL RUBBER ENDS UP AMID KOREA SALE, RUPIAH WATCH.
newsitem.headline: KL RUBBER ENDS UP AMID KOREA SALE, RUPIAH WATCH.

text.p: Malaysian rubber prices ended up on Thursday, with government trade sources reporting a SMR20 sale to South Korea.
Market dealers, however, said a correction was due soon because of the weakness of the rupiah, which could drag down prices of both Indonesian and Malaysian rubber.

Trade sources in the Malaysian Rubber Exchange and Licensing Board (MRELB) reported hearing on Thursday that about 10 containers of the SMR20 was sold by a private broker to a South Korean client at 250 cents a kg for September shipment.
But dealers said they had no confirmation of the sale.
"With the market lethargy we have now, no one's bothered to check a small sale like this," said a trader.

Indonesia's central bank, Bank Indonesia, said on Thursday it will no longer announce its daily intervention and conversion bands for the rupiah, causing the currency to plunge to a new low against the dollar.
Indonesian rubber prices were not immediately affected by the news, but dealers said the market could come up under pressure eventually from buyers expecting cheaper prices.
